column1: # Courier test kit: the hand-written MIME samples, one <name>.eml beside this file per row. Tab-separated, UTF-8.
# Columns: name, outcome, subject, from, attachments, word, family.
#   outcome      ok (read), refused:<reason> (too_large, too_deep, too_many_parts, timeout, malformed, too_complex),
#                or either (broken input a parser may read or cleanly refuse; nothing else is checked).
#   subject      the decoded subject: unfolded (CRLF removed, folding whitespace kept), RFC 2047 words decoded, the space
#                between adjacent encoded words dropped, control and bidi-override characters stripped as the store does.
#                Empty: the message has no Subject. "-": not checked.
#   from         the lowercase address of the first From mailbox; nobody@invalid when there is none. "-": not checked.
#   attachments  leaf parts a reader sees as attachments: every leaf except the body (the first text/plain and first
#                text/html with no file name and not marked attachment) and parts marked Content-Disposition: inline;
#                a message/rfc822 part counts once and is not descended. "-": not checked.
#   word         lowercase, at least 4 letters, in the decoded body text (text/plain, or the HTML's visible text when
#                there is no text/plain), compared ignoring case. "-": not checked.
#   family       basic, charset, encoding, header, structure, attachment, html, links, bulk, malformed or limits.
# Limits: 2,000 MIME entities (the message and every multipart counted), multiparts nested 20 deep (the message's own
# counted), 40 MiB a message, 10 s a parse. The first 27 rows are deskd's samples (courier/mime in deskd's tests).
